pairs.why: A's orange rim turns softly from light to a darker underside with a soft cast shadow on the wall, like the real clock. B's rim is flatter and sits on a hard floor shadow that the real card doesn't have.
B's navy body has a broad soft turn from light to shadow and a gentle bounce of colored light at the lens, like the real lamp. A's tiny body shows little modeling.
Both use the same soft matte light and the same gentle form shadows, so lighting gives no reason to choose.
A's dark body and keys keep a soft, low-glare form turn like the real calculator. B's pale glossy keys add sharper highlights and a much wider value range.
B has slightly more shadow depth on the arch and door, closer to the real door's side shading, but the difference is small.
A's metal head has smoother, broader sheen and gentler shading, like the real viewer. B's cast shadows on the floor are crisper.
A has a deeper shadow side on the cap and a darker cast shadow on the floor, closer to the real card's strong light-to-shadow drop.
Both have similar soft leaf shading and a similar cast shadow on the sand, so lighting gives no clear reason to choose.
